---
title: "Scientific solver reference"
---

These functions expose numerical primitives. The [public class API](api.qmd) handles frame extraction, trained models and result stores. Positions use centred pitch metres, velocities m/s, time seconds and angles radians. Low-level solver defaults can differ from the class defaults; pass explicit settings when reproducing a calculation.

## Pitch control

Import `integrate_pitch_control` from `PRESS.model`.

```python
integrate_pitch_control(r_grid, p_pos, p_vel, ball_carrier_idx, T_ball,
    lambda_control=4.3, s=0.45, v_max=5.0, a_max=5.0,
    t_max_pc=8.0, dt_pc=0.01, tol=1e-6,
    integration_method="exponential")
```

`r_grid` is `(N,2)` candidate positions; `p_pos` and `p_vel` are `(M,2)` players; `ball_carrier_idx` identifies the excluded carrier; `T_ball` is `(N,)` ball-arrival time. `lambda_control` is a rate in inverse seconds, `s` arrival dispersion in seconds, and `v_max`/`a_max` the motion settings. Returns player-by-target control **`(M,N)`**. Control begins when the ball arrives. Exponential Euler allocates the available uncontrolled mass exactly for rates frozen over each step, preserving total control at most one; it is first order for time-varying rates. The full configured horizon is used, including partial final steps. `tol` is a compatibility argument and no longer changes the integration schedule. Sum attacking rows, then use the saved isotonic map through `PassRiskModel` or the public class. `integration_method="euler"` is an explicit numerical sensitivity; archived sources preserve the original clipped solver. [Mathematics and frame example](vignettes/02_pass_probability/02_pass_probability.ipynb). [@spearman2017; @spearman2018beyond]

## Pass probability along a trajectory

Import from `PRESS.model.solver_pitch_control`.

```python
integrate_pass_prob(p_pos, p_vel, attacker_idx, ball_carrier_idx,
    ball_trajectory, lambda_control=4.3, s=0.45, v_max=5.0,
    a_max=5.0, dt=0.04, z_max=2.0, tol=1e-6,
    integration_method="exponential")
```

`p_pos`, `p_vel` are `(M,2)`; `attacker_idx` selects attacking rows; `ball_trajectory` is `(T,3)` with x, y and height sampled every `dt`. Control accumulates at or below `z_max` metres; the carrier is excluded before sharing mass. Returns scalar attacking success. Each supplied sample starts one integration interval: the benchmark's 251 samples at 0..10 s retain its historical 10.04 s left-step schedule. There is no parameter-dependent cutoff. This reconstructed-path likelihood estimates parameters; candidate-field inference uses target PPCF and its separately fitted isotonic map. [Pass vignette](vignettes/02_pass_probability/02_pass_probability.ipynb).

## Drive-loss integration

Import `integrate_loss_prob` from `PRESS.model`.

```python
integrate_loss_prob(p_pos, p_vel, x_bc0, v_bc0, delta_t,
    lambda_0, beta_v, beta_B, s=0.45, v_max=5.0, a_max=7.0,
    dt=0.04, tol=1e-6, pitch_length=105.0, pitch_width=68.0,
    max_time=None, integration_method="exponential")
```

`p_pos`, `p_vel` describe `(M,2)` defenders; carrier position/velocity are `(2,)`; `delta_t` is the integration horizon. The default uses exponential Euler: with frozen cause hazards, it assigns only the available survival mass, via `S * (1 - exp(-H * dt))`, split in proportion to cause hazards. `integration_method="euler"` reproduces the historical update for comparison. Rates are evaluated again each step; stability does not imply timestep convergence. See [exponential integrators](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0962492910000048). The last integration step stops at the requested horizon, including nonmultiples of `dt`. For row-specific durations under JIT/vmap, supply a static `max_time` at least as large as every duration (1 s for the rate-training cohort); otherwise `delta_t` must be static. The intensity is `lambda_0 * exp(beta_v * carrier_speed + beta_B * minimum_boundary_distance)`, combined with defender arrival and shared remaining survival mass. Returns `(M,)` defender-specific cause probabilities; their sum is total drive loss. The [drive vignette](vignettes/01_ball_drive_risk/01_ball_drive_risk.ipynb) executes this primitive and the frame-level class method. Intensity specification is **own derivation**; motion/control concepts are inspired by the cited literature.

## Ball flight and receiver arrival

Import `time_flight` from `PRESS.physics`.

```python
time_flight(r_bc, r_target, p_attackers, v_attackers,
    v0_candidates=linspace(10,30,20),
    theta_candidates=linspace(0,pi/3,20),
    t_max_flight=10.0, dt_ball=0.04, grid_step=0.5,
    v_max=5.0, a_max=5.0, z_max=2.0,
    rho=1.2, Cd=0.25, A=0.038, m=0.43, g=9.81,
    distance_mode="exact")
```

The `linspace` notation describes default JAX arrays. Carrier position is `(2,)`; targets `(N,2)`; receivers `(M,2)`. The receiver nearest in initial position to each target supplies the desired arrival time. A candidate flight is selected by matching that time, subject to reachability and controllable height. Exact target distances are the default; `distance_mode="lookup"` enables the corrected regular radial grid as an approximation. `grid_step` affects that approximation only. Drag parameters are air density `rho`, drag coefficient `Cd`, cross-section `A`, mass `m`, and gravity `g`, in SI units. Returns `(N,)` flight times. No receiver or reachable candidate gives infinite time and zero control. The class uses its saved flight configuration; see [its defaults](api.qmd#pitch-control-and-pass-success).

The flight ODE includes gravity and constant-coefficient aerodynamic drag. Below 5 cm while descending, height is held and horizontal aerodynamic drag continues; there is no bounce, fitted rolling friction or Magnus force. The latent vertical velocity is not reset by this ODE and is not interpreted as a post-impact velocity. The model consumes simulated positions and height. [Flight equations and assumptions](vignettes/02_pass_probability/02_pass_probability.ipynb).

These numerical functions expect valid, compatible arrays and physical parameters. They do not validate canonical match tables or manage dependency caches. Prefer the class APIs when the task is to compute a frame of a possession.


## Uniform final pass TTI

The pretrained run41 pass model uses `v_max=5.5`, `a_max=7`, `a_turn=7` and `preserve_initial_overspeed=True` consistently. The lower-level trajectory and target-control solvers accept the same `a_turn` and `preserve_initial_overspeed` keyword arguments. Their compatibility defaults remain unchanged; pass the fitted artifact settings to reproduce it. Physical λ,s are MLE estimates along reconstructed paths; isotonic knots are learned separately on cross-fitted hypothetical PPCF scores.
